quotes.def: Where a significant aspect of what someone does depends on factors beyond his control, yet we continue to treat him in that respect as an object of moral judgment, it can be called moral luck.
quotes.circ: luck in one's circumstances – the kind of problems and situations one faces.
quotes.known: It is possible also to assess the decision from the point of view of what could be known at the time, but this is not the end of the story.
quotes.subtract: it seems rational to subtract the effects of occurrences subsequent to the choice, that were merely possible at the time, and concentrate moral assessment on the actual decision in light of the probabilities.
quotes.actual: We judge people for what they actually do or fail to do, not just for what they would have done if circumstances had been different.
quotes.driver: The driver, if he is entirely without fault, will feel terrible about his role in the event, but will not have to reproach himself.
quotes.fate: It amounts to holding them responsible for the contributions of fate as well as for their own
quotes.shrink: The area of genuine agency, and therefore of legitimate moral judgment, seems to shrink under this scrutiny to an extensionless point.
